newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian stock market sets up Web site.
newsitem.headline: Italian stock market sets up Web site.

text.p: The Italian stock exchange said it had set up a web site on the Internet for brokers and fund managers to access financial market information, which will start from November 8.
The stock market council said in a statement the site would provide information on a range of stock market subjects.

These include exchange information, members, contacts and general market statistics; market data on individual shares, derivatives, indices and macroecononic data; listed company information; brokers, investment firms and bank data; and options and futures data.

"The broader purpose of the development is to disseminate information about the increasingly important Italian market to a growing international audience of bank brokers, trading and fund managers," it said.

Average daily turnover on the Italian stock market has grown nine percent in 1996 to 613 billion lire and 12 new companies listed in the first 10 months of the year, while total market capitalisation is up 13 percent at 367 trillion lire.

On the derivatives side, the stock market said average daily volume in futures was up 119 percent at 10,024 contracts per day in October while options volume had risen 254 percent to 1,479 contracts per day.
